source.exact_title: Anti-Inflammatory Effects of Curcumin in the Inflammatory Diseases: Status, Limitations and Countermeasures

consistency_findings: Table 1 and disease-specific narrative sections sometimes restate the same cited study; extraction prioritizes row-level table atoms and uses narrative atoms only for cross-cutting synthesis or explicit limitations to reduce duplicate evidence objects.

For reference 139, Table 2 lists SinaCurcumin 40 mg twice daily for 2 weeks, whereas the COVID-19 narrative describes an oral nano-curcumin dose of 80 mg twice daily. The source-level discrepancy is retained and not reconciled.
The review contains both positive and null/uncertain clinical summaries (for example psoriasis, depression, and atherosclerosis); these were retained rather than reconciled away.

The Table 1 post-traumatic osteoarthritis row combines curcumin and curcumin nanoparticles under reference 57; the atom preserves that combined presentation instead of splitting it into unsupported separate studies.
schema_gaps: The governing LiteratureAtom model is oriented to primary literature and has no dedicated narrative-review synthesis atom kind.

Study-level results summarized by this review are encoded as qualitative_result with tags secondary_reported_result and ref_N; they are not represented as if the review enrolled participants or generated those results.
The schema has no first-class field for the review citation number that supports a secondary report, so citation numbers are preserved in tags and source-anchor table rows.
The schema does not represent review search strategy, evidence grading, or risk-of-bias judgments; those issues are handled in SEA appraisal instead of being invented as atom data.
protocol_version_note: The project file named summary-evaluation-appraisal-protocol-v4-compact.md identifies itself internally as Integrated Compact v3. The file was followed as the designated governing SEA source, and this naming/version mismatch is reported rather than silently resolved.
extraction_limitations: The source is a narrative review, not a primary study. ATOM therefore captures the review authors’ synthesis and table-reported secondary evidence with explicit secondary-source tags.

The review rarely provides effect estimates, confidence intervals, denominators, or complete trial design details in its summary tables; directional outcomes were not converted into quantitative_result atoms.
Pure bibliography entries were excluded from atomization and were instead converted into the separate 184-item reference task queue.
The publisher advertisement on page 4525 was excluded as non-substantive content.
No external evidence was used to upgrade or correct the review’s clinical claims; COVID-19 claims are preserved as historical 2021 source content.
